problem: Remote object grounding benchmarks (REVERIE, FAO/SOON) assume a totally unseen environment and use specialized navigation architectures; they ignore that household robots operate in the same space for years and can pre-explore and map it. Generic 2D vision-language scorers also cannot directly rank 100,000s of 3D object proposals.
motivation: In a familiar environment, locating a referred object reduces to choosing the best-matching proposal among all stored proposals (up to ~100k). The authors show that a generic VL backbone (ViLBERT) with a few 3D and training/inference tricks can do this and beat specialized VLN models, and it transfers to a real robot.
key_idea: Fine-tune a generic ViLBERT scorer with 3D positional embeddings, context proposals and negative-viewpoint augmentation, then explore locally up to L steps, score proposals in viewpoint groups, and take the global argmax as the referent.
insight: Handling the huge search space matters most: removing viewpoint grouping drops val-unseen RGS from 43.75 to 10.17, removing negative-viewpoint augmentation drops it to 14.14, and removing the distance limit drops it to 31.50. 3D positional encoding and context proposals give smaller gains (40.50 and 35.64 without them), and the type of 3D encoding matters little. 3D coordinates alone did not teach the network a distance limit, since L steps do not map cleanly to Euclidean distance.
method: 3D positional embeddings: replace 2D box coordinates with (x,y,z,r), where r is half the 3D box diagonal, with xyz normalized relative to the viewpoint that observed the region

Context proposals and neighborhood features: add Mask-RCNN proposals (at headings 0/90/180/270) to reach 400 regions per viewpoint, plus average features of the 100 nearest viewpoints as extra regions

Viewpoint negative augmentation: train with sigmoid/BCE loss per region, using the ground-truth viewpoint or, with probability R=80%, a random negative viewpoint, so scores are calibrated at inference
Non-exhaustive frontier exploration: explore only up to L steps from the start (L=8 REVERIE, L=13 FAO), counting exploration path plus shortest path to the prediction in TL/SPL
Inference-time viewpoint grouping: score each viewpoint's regions as a separate batch with the query, then take the global argmax across viewpoints
Pre-exploration variant (PE): use a pre-built map so the path excludes exploration and only the direct path to the target counts
Real robot: TurtleBot3 builds a map with Mask-RCNN regions with depth-derived 3D coordinates; RREx-BoT selects a region from a speech query and ROS navigation drives to it

setting.backbone: ViLBERT (pretrained on Conceptual Captions, fine-tuned) as a region scorer; Mask-RCNN for context proposals
setting.training_data: REVERIE train (10,466 instructions) and FAO/SOON train (26,790 instructions), with region proposals from REVERIE/DUET plus Mask-RCNN; 160 epochs on REVERIE, 30 on FAO, on one T4 GPU for 4 days
setting.observation: panoramic RGB-D at each viewpoint, region proposals with median-depth 3D positions
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (frontier exploration, then shortest path to the predicted object)
setting.privileged: none for the base model (explores up to L steps); the PE variant uses a pre-explored map; L is tuned from training path lengths and validation performance; REVERIE/DUET-provided object proposals are used

numbers_note: FAO is a differently named benchmark (SOON), labelled other:FAO (SOON). Test-unseen FAO RGS is not reported. The FAO PE val-unseen row (SR 49.17, RGS 11.06, SPL 48.63, RGSPL 11.06) was omitted.
results: On REVERIE test-unseen, RREx-BoT reaches RGS 42.07 vs 32.23 for AutoVLN (no pre-exploration) and 34.69 for OSMaN (with pre-exploration), and SR 65.18. On FAO it reaches SR 47.53 on test vs 40.36 for AutoVLN. Path-weighted metrics (SPL/RGSPL) are very low when exploration is counted; with pre-exploration they exceed OSMaN (SPL 62.04 vs 47.78).
limitations: Exploration inflates path length, giving very low SPL/RGSPL (e.g. TL 177-339 m) unless the environment is pre-explored
Depends on provided object proposals and a tuned exploration limit L, chosen per dataset; language understanding is weak for long instructions; real-robot demo is qualitative only, with no numbers
